report.verdict: Michigan's regulated online market booked $355.7m of combined iGaming + online sports betting gross receipts in September 2026 (+17.5% YoY, +5.4% MoM) with iGaming ($300.2m GR / $288.2m AGR, +18.4% YoY) doing almost all of the work and OSB AGR up 88% on an easy, promo-heavy comp. The rules are stable today but every swing factor sits in 2027: the iGaming free-play deduction falls to zero on 1 Jan 2027, a new governor inherits a structural budget gap that the outgoing administration tried to plug with a 36% top iGaming tier and a per-bet levy, and the market remains closed to new entrants absent a Detroit-casino or tribal skin.

kpis.label: Detroit casinos slots + tables AGR, Sep-26

summary: **Market size (online): $355.7m of combined internet gaming and online sports betting gross receipts in September 2026**, per the Michigan Gaming Control Board (MGCB) release of 22 Oct 2026 — +5.4% on August ($337.6m) and +17.5% on September 2025 ($302.7m). On the taxable (adjusted gross receipts, AGR) basis the market was $313.0m, +22.0% YoY. Jan–Sep 2026 online GR is $3,175.7m (+18.9% YoY).

**iGaming is the engine: $300.2m GR and $288.2m AGR in September (+15.9% / +18.4% YoY).** The −0.9% MoM print is purely calendar (30 vs 31 days); AGR per day rose 2.4% to $9.6m. YTD iGaming AGR is $2,600.9m (+23.3%), and the trailing-12-month (Oct-25 to Sep-26) AGR is $3,392.6m — Michigan is tracking to the first $3.5bn+ iGaming AGR year in any US state.

**OSB is mature and promo-driven: handle $544.8m (+3.9% YoY), GR $55.5m (+27.3% YoY) on a 10.2% hold, AGR $24.9m (+88.2% YoY).** The AGR jump reflects promo deductions falling to 55% of GR from 70% a year ago; YTD OSB AGR is actually down 6.9% to $242.8m because promo deductions ran at 48% of GR YTD vs 39% in 2025. Handle growth of 5.8% YTD says the sportsbook customer base is largely built out.

**Online dominates the MGCB-reported market: 77% of September's $459.3m of reported gross gaming revenue** (iGaming $300.2m + OSB $55.5m + Detroit slots/tables $102.8m + Detroit retail sportsbook $0.8m). Caveat: Michigan's 23 tribal land-based casinos do not publish revenue and the Michigan Lottery (incl. iLottery) sits outside the MGCB, so true online penetration of all gambling is lower — n/a.

**Retail is flat-to-low-growth: Detroit's three casinos reported $102.8m of slots/table AGR (+4.7% YoY, +2.3% YTD)**, split MGM Grand 47% / MotorCity 32% / Hollywood Casino at Greektown 21%; retail sportsbook QAGR was just $0.77m on $12.4m handle — the on-property book is a rounding error at 1.4% of OSB AGR.

**Tax regime (iGaming): graduated 20–28% of AGR** (28% marginal above $12m annual AGR — every one of the 15 operators sits in the top tier), plus a 1.25% City of Detroit wagering tax for the three commercial licensees (29.25% all-in). The tax base is GR less a capped free-play deduction: 4% of GR in 2026 (year 5), and **zero from 1 January 2027** under MCL 432.303(a) — a structural ~1.1pt-of-GR increase in effective tax (~$40m/yr at a $3.6bn GR run-rate; our estimate).

**Tax regime (OSB): 8.4% of AGR** (+1.25% city for Detroit casinos), with promotional/free-play deductions **uncapped** — the reason state OSB tax was only $1.8m in September on $55.5m of GR (3.3% of GR; 7.4% of AGR). Fantasy contests are taxed at 8.4% of adjusted revenue; Detroit casinos pay 8.1% state + 10.9% city on slots/tables.

**Tax take: operators paid $62.4m to the State in September (iGaming $60.6m, OSB $1.8m; +20.9% YoY)**, $14.0m to the City of Detroit (iGaming $13.5m, OSB $0.55m) and $8.3m to tribal local governing bodies. YTD state online receipts are $557.5m (+24.7%); fiscal-year 2026 (Oct-25 to Sep-26) iGaming state tax/payments reached $703.9m and OSB $31.0m (our aggregation of MGCB monthly files). Remaining Internet Gaming Fund balances flow to the School Aid Fund.

**Licensing is a closed, skin-limited system: 15 operator licences (3 Detroit casinos + 12 federally recognised tribes), one platform each**; all 15 offer iGaming and 13 offer OSB. Fees under the Lawful Internet Gaming Act / Lawful Sports Betting Act are modest — $50,000 application, $100,000 initial licence, $50,000 annual (5-year term); suppliers $5,000/$5,000/$2,500 — but there is no path to market without displacing an incumbent platform partner.

**Operator landscape (iGaming AGR share, Sep-26): FanDuel 24.7%, BetMGM 21.1%, DraftKings 14.9%, BetRivers 7.5%, Fanatics 6.7%, Hard Rock Bet 6.4%, Caesars/WSOP 5.2%**, with Golden Nugget, theScore Bet, bet365, BetPARX, FireKeepers (NeoGames), Soaring Eagle (GAN), Caesars Horseshoe and Four Winds (Strive) making up the remaining 13.6%. Top-3 concentration is 60.7%, down from 67.9% a year ago as Hard Rock Bet (relaunched on the Hannahville licence in Dec-25), Fanatics and bet365 took share from FanDuel (−2.2pt) and BetMGM (−4.3pt).

**OSB is a duopoly-plus: FanDuel 34.2% and DraftKings 28.2% of September handle (62.4% combined), BetMGM 10.4%, Fanatics 9.0%, bet365 5.5%.** Promo intensity is extreme at the challengers — bet365 deducted 129% of its GR (negative AGR of −$1.3m) and Hard Rock Bet 93%, versus 51–53% at FanDuel/DraftKings and 36% at BetMGM.

**Tribal vs commercial: tribal-licensed skins generated 51.6% of September iGaming AGR ($148.6m vs $139.6m).** Tribal payments are routed 70% Internet Gaming Fund / 10% Michigan Strategic Fund / 20% local governing body; commercial tax goes 65% IGF / 5% Agriculture Equine Industry Development Fund (capped $3m) / 30% City of Detroit, and the IGF carries a first-call guarantee to top up Detroit if the city's gaming tax receipts fall below $183m.

**Fiscal politics are the key regulatory risk and they just reset.** Gov. Whitmer's FY2027 executive budget (11 Feb 2026) proposed a 36% top iGaming tier above $185m AGR, a $0.25/$0.50 per-wager OSB levy (~$38.8m) and elimination of the OSB promo deduction (~$21.1m) — ~$195–200m in total. The Senate stripped all three in May 2026 (bipartisan) and the FY2027 budget was signed on 21 Jul 2026 with no gaming-tax change. Whitmer is term-limited; preliminary results show Jocelyn Benson (D) winning the 3 Nov 2026 governor's race, and the FY2028 executive budget (Feb 2027) is the next test.

**Enforcement is the most aggressive of any US state on prediction markets.** The Attorney General sued Kalshi under the Lawful Sports Betting Act in March 2026, won a TRO (29 Jun, $120k/day) and a preliminary injunction (2 Sep); Robinhood (Sep), Coinbase (7 Oct) and Polymarket/QCX LLC (28 Oct, positions closed by 25 Nov 2026) have all agreed to halt sports event contracts in Michigan. MGCB also issued 32 cease-and-desist letters to offshore sites on 8 Oct 2026 and treats sweepstakes casinos as illegal gaming under MCL 432.

**Product scope is widening at the margin: MGCB added fixed-odds horse racing to the OSB catalogue on 30 Oct 2026**, allowing licensed online books to offer fixed-price race bets alongside pari-mutuel — modest handle but a signal that the regulator is willing to expand the catalogue administratively rather than legislatively.

**Responsible gambling framework is statutory and funded:** 21+ age, geolocation, self-exclusion via the Internet Gaming and Sports Betting Responsible Gaming Database (plus the Disassociated Persons List for casinos), free Gamban licences for residents, 1-800-GAMBLER on all materials, and $500,000 a year each from the Internet Gaming and Internet Sports Betting Funds to the Compulsive Gaming Prevention Fund. Payment-method statistics are not published by MGCB (n/a).

**Read-through for an operator weighing Michigan:** this is the deepest, most profitable iGaming pool in the US (c.$3.4bn TTM AGR, 28% headline tax with no city levy for tribal skins), but entry is only via acquiring or replacing an incumbent platform on one of 15 licences; the 2027 free-play sunset and a probable renewed tax push argue for underwriting at ≥30% effective iGaming tax and for OSB as a customer-acquisition channel rather than a profit centre (8.4% nominal, but 48% of GR is being handed back in promos YTD).

**Benchmark check:** the lead trade-press article (Gaming Intelligence, 27 Oct 2026) headlines the same $355.7m / +18% figure; our YoY of +17.5% uses the MGCB's September 2025 release ($302.7m) rather than rounded figures. All headline numbers reconcile to the MGCB operator-level workbooks to within $0.1m.

segments.name: iGaming (online casino & poker)
segments.headline: $288.2m AGR, +18.4% YoY: the largest and fastest-compounding regulated iGaming pool in the US, with share drifting from the FanDuel/BetMGM duopoly to Hard Rock, Fanatics and bet365.
narrative: **September gross receipts were $300.2m and AGR $288.2m**, the first time Michigan iGaming has cleared $300m of GR in a 30-day month. The −0.9% MoM optics are a calendar artefact: August had 31 days; on a per-day basis AGR rose 2.4% to $9.6m. YoY growth of +18.4% (AGR) is slightly above the +17.6% printed in August and well above the Detroit land-based market (+4.7%), so cannibalisation arguments remain unsupported by the data — retail is growing, just slowly. Year-to-date AGR is $2,600.9m (+23.3%) against $2,109.6m in Jan–Sep 2025; calendar 2025 closed at $2,901.3m AGR and $3,087.0m GR, and the Oct-25 to Sep-26 fiscal year reached $3,392.6m AGR and $3,552.7m GR. On the current run-rate calendar 2026 AGR lands around $3.5–3.6bn (our estimate, not an MGCB figure).

**The taxable base is tightening on a statutory timetable.** AGR equals GR less free play wagered by players, but the Lawful Internet Gaming Act caps that deduction at 10% of GR in years 1–3, 6% in year 4, 4% in year 5 and 0% from year 6 (MCL 432.303(a)), with year 1 defined as the January following launch. For the January-2021 launch cohort that means 6% in 2025 (observed: 6.1% of GR in Sep-25), 4% in 2026 (observed: 4.0% in Sep-26) and **nil from 1 January 2027**. The arithmetic is mechanical: at 28% marginal tax the sunset lifts effective tax by ~1.1 points of GR, roughly $40m a year at a $3.6bn GR run-rate (our estimate), and it does so without any legislative vote. Operators whose promotional economics rely on free play will either absorb the cost or cut bonusing; expect the GR-to-AGR gap to collapse to zero in the January 2027 release.

**Tax paid to the State was $60.6m in September (+19.3% YoY)** and $538.7m YTD (+24.6%). Reconciling the MGCB workbook: commercial AGR of $139.6m attracted a 28% liability of $39.1m, of which 70% ($27.4m) went to the State (65% Internet Gaming Fund + 5% Agriculture Equine Industry Development Fund) and 30% ($11.7m) plus the 1.25% city wagering tax ($1.7m) to Detroit — matching the reported $13.5m. Tribal AGR of $148.6m carried a $41.6m liability split 80% to the State ($33.3m: 70% IGF + 10% Michigan Strategic Fund) and 20% ($8.3m) to the tribes' local governing bodies. Total iGaming tax burden including the city levy was therefore $82.4m, or 28.6% of AGR and 27.5% of GR — the second-highest effective iGaming rate among US states after Pennsylvania, but with no slot/table differential and no separate poker rate.

**Share is fragmenting at the top.** FanDuel (MotorCity licence) led with $71.3m AGR / 24.7% share (vs 26.9% in Sep-25) and BetMGM (MGM Grand Detroit) $60.8m / 21.1% (vs 25.4%); DraftKings (Bay Mills) $43.0m / 14.9% (vs 15.6%). The share went to **Hard Rock Bet**, which the MGCB notes ceased operating on the Hannahville licence in July 2025 and resumed in December 2025 (booking $33.6m AGR in its first month and $18.6m / 6.4% in September), **Fanatics** (Lac Vieux Desert, ex-PointsBet) at $19.2m / 6.7% (vs 5.4%) and **bet365** on the Little Traverse Bay Bands licence at $6.3m / 2.2% (vs 0.7% a year earlier under the prior platform). BetRivers (Little River) is steady at $21.7m / 7.5%; Caesars/WSOP (Grand Traverse) slipped to $14.9m / 5.2% and fell 10.7% MoM. The tail — Golden Nugget $9.2m, theScore Bet (Hollywood Casino at Greektown, replacing the ESPN BET/Barstool branding) $7.5m, BetPARX $4.2m, FireKeepers/NeoGames $4.2m, Soaring Eagle/GAN $3.4m, Caesars Horseshoe (Sault Ste. Marie, replacing Wynn) $2.3m and Four Winds/Strive $1.6m — is sub-scale but every one of them clears the $12m annual AGR threshold and pays 28% at the margin.

**Commercial implication.** Michigan is the best-evidenced case that a 28% GGR tax, one skin per licence and a 15-licence cap can coexist with 18–23% growth five years post-launch. For a would-be entrant the constraint is not economics but access: there are no unallocated licences, so entry means buying or displacing a platform partner (the Hard Rock/Hannahville, bet365/LTBB and Caesars Horseshoe/Sault Ste. Marie transitions show this is possible, typically with a tribal licensee). Underwrite at ≥30% all-in tax from 2027, assume no free-play shelter, and note that tribal skins avoid the 1.25% Detroit levy and route 20% of their payment to a local governing body — a relationship cost that is part of the deal, not a tax.

segments.name: Online sports betting (OSB)
segments.headline: $544.8m handle, 10.2% hold, $24.9m AGR: NFL kick-off lifted GR 27% YoY but 55% of it was handed back as promos — Michigan OSB is a low-tax, low-margin acquisition channel, not a profit pool.
narrative: **Handle of $544.8m was +64.9% MoM on the NFL/college-football restart but only +3.9% YoY** (Sep-25: $524.4m), and YTD handle of $3,876.1m is +5.8%. Michigan's sportsbook has effectively reached maturity on volume; growth is coming from hold, which was 10.2% in September (8.3% a year earlier) and 12.0% YTD (11.6% in 2025) as parlay and same-game-parlay mix deepens. Gross receipts were $55.5m (+27.3% YoY), $465.8m YTD (+9.3%). The month-to-month hold volatility that defined 2025 (14.9% in January, 6.9% in March) persists; September 2026 hold ranged from 5.8% at Caesars to 15.8% at Hard Rock Bet.

**The taxable base is being hollowed out by promotions.** Under the Lawful Sports Betting Act, AGR is GR less free play and promotional credits with **no cap** — unlike iGaming. In September operators deducted $30.6m (55.2% of GR) to arrive at $24.9m AGR; a year ago the deduction was 69.7%, which is why AGR is +88.2% YoY on a GR gain of only 27%. YTD the picture reverses: deductions ran at 47.9% of GR versus 38.8% in 2025, so YTD AGR fell 6.9% to $242.8m even as GR rose 9.3%. The challengers are driving it — bet365 deducted $6.0m against $4.7m of GR (AGR −$1.3m), Hard Rock Bet 92.7% of GR, Caesars 56.0% — while FanDuel (50.6%) and DraftKings (52.7%) are also running hot into the NFL season. Operators with negative AGR pay no tax and receive no credit, which is why the State's OSB take ($1.8m, 7.4% of aggregate AGR) sits below the 8.4% headline.

**Tax: 8.4% of AGR, plus 1.25% of AGR to the City of Detroit for the three commercial licensees** (9.65% all-in; 8.4% for tribal skins). Distribution is 65% Internet Sports Betting Fund / 5% AEIDF (≤$3m) / 30% Detroit for commercial, 90% ISBF / 10% Michigan Strategic Fund for tribal. September's State take was $1.83m (+138% YoY, +13.7% MoM), Detroit's $0.55m; YTD State receipts are $18.8m (+26.1%) and calendar 2025 was $27.1m on $435.9m AGR. Governor Whitmer's FY2027 budget papers described the 8.4% rate as 28th of 30 legal states and the lowest among Michigan's neighbours, and proposed (i) a $0.25 per-wager charge on an operator's first 20m bets and $0.50 thereafter (~$38.8m/yr) and (ii) eliminating the promo deduction (~$21.1m/yr). Both were stripped by the Senate in May 2026 and are absent from the FY2027 budget signed 21 Jul 2026 — but the revenue case has now been written, scored and published, and a per-wager levy on 2025's 5.4bn-dollar / high-frequency handle would fall disproportionately on the FanDuel/DraftKings micro-bet model.

**Concentration is the highest of any Michigan vertical.** FanDuel took $186.3m of handle (34.2%) and DraftKings $153.7m (28.2%); BetMGM $56.6m (10.4%, but 20.6% of AGR on a 14.0% hold and lighter promos), Fanatics $48.9m (9.0%, up from 8.7% under PointsBet), bet365 $30.1m (5.5%), Caesars $21.3m (3.9%), Hard Rock Bet $20.0m (3.7%), theScore Bet $15.2m (2.8%), BetRivers $9.1m (1.7%); GAN, BetPARX, FireKeepers and Four Winds share the final 0.7%. Thirteen of the 15 licensees run a sportsbook — Golden Nugget and Caesars Horseshoe do not. Note the distribution of economics: FanDuel+DraftKings hold 62% of handle but only 60% of AGR; BetMGM converts 10% of handle into 21% of AGR.

**Catalogue and competition.** On 30 Oct 2026 the MGCB added fixed-odds horse racing to the OSB catalogue, letting licensed books offer locked-price race bets alongside pari-mutuel — small handle, but it is the first material product expansion since launch and was done administratively. More consequential is the removal of unlicensed substitutes: Kalshi (court-ordered), Robinhood, Coinbase and Polymarket have all withdrawn sports event contracts from Michigan between June and October 2026, with Polymarket's open positions to be closed by 25 Nov 2026. If those venues were taking even low-single-digit share of sports-outcome dollars, Q4 2026 licensed handle should show a modest tailwind; we would read any YoY handle acceleration above the ~4–6% trend in Oct–Dec as evidence.

**Commercial implication.** Michigan OSB offers the lowest effective tax of any large US online state (3.3% of GR in September after promos) and 10%+ structural hold, but the two incumbents' promotional cadence sets the price of share. A new skin without a national brand (see bet365 and Hard Rock's negative-to-nil AGR) is buying customers for iGaming cross-sell, and should be modelled that way: Michigan OSB AGR of $242.8m YTD is 9% of iGaming AGR.

segments.name: Retail: Detroit casinos, retail sportsbooks, tribal casinos & fantasy
segments.headline: Detroit's three casinos grew slots/tables AGR 4.7% YoY to $102.8m with MGM at 47% share; retail sportsbooks are vestigial and tribal land-based revenue is unpublished.
narrative: **Detroit's commercial casinos reported $103.55m of aggregate revenue for September 2026**: $102.78m from slots and table games (+4.7% YoY, −5.6% MoM, +2.3% YTD) and $0.77m of qualified AGR from retail sports betting. MGM Grand Detroit earned $48.84m (+6.5% YoY, 47% share), MotorCity $32.6m (+12.7%, 32%) and Hollywood Casino at Greektown $21.34m (−8.8%, 21%). The market is growing at roughly a quarter of the online rate and share is consolidating toward MGM and MotorCity — the same two groups whose online skins (BetMGM, FanDuel) lead iGaming, which is consistent with omnichannel loyalty programmes rather than online-to-retail substitution.

**Retail tax is heavier than online on paper but lighter in cash.** Detroit casinos pay an 8.1% State wagering tax ($8.3m in September vs $8.0m a year earlier) and a 10.9% city wagering tax plus development-agreement payments ($12.7m to the City), i.e. ~20% of AGR all-in. Retail sportsbooks pay 8.4% plus 1.25% to the city: $30,922 to the State and $37,793 to Detroit in September on $12.39m of handle and $784,762 of gross receipts (6.3% hold). MGM's retail book posted a negative $48,265 QAGR; MotorCity ($602,755) and Greektown ($215,281) carried the segment. Retail sportsbook QAGR is 3% of the online figure and has no strategic weight beyond on-property amenity.

**Tribal land-based gaming is the unreported half of the retail market.** Twelve federally recognised tribes operate 23 casinos under state compacts administered by the MGCB's tribal gaming section; revenue is not published (n/a), and the tribes' only public footprint in the MGCB statistics is through their online skins ($148.6m of iGaming AGR, 51.6% of the total) and the 20% share of their iGaming payment routed to local governing bodies ($8.3m in September, $72.1m YTD). For an operator, the tribal licence is the realistic entry route — 12 of the 15 online licences are tribal, and the Hard Rock, bet365, Caesars Horseshoe and Fanatics platform changes all occurred on tribal paper.

**Fantasy contests** are a licensed but immaterial vertical: operators reported $657,854 of adjusted revenue for August 2026 and paid $55,260 in tax at 8.4%, all to the Fantasy Contest Fund. The Michigan Lottery, including its iLottery products, is regulated separately and is excluded from every figure in this report (n/a).

segments.name: Licensing & tax regime
segments.headline: Fifteen single-skin licences, cheap fees, a 28% graduated iGaming tax (29.25% in Detroit) and 8.4% on OSB — stable since 2021, with the free-play sunset on 1 Jan 2027 the only scheduled change and a rejected $200m tax package the live political one.
narrative: **Legal framework.** Online gaming operates under the Lawful Internet Gaming Act (PA 152 of 2019, MCL 432.301–432.322) and the Lawful Sports Betting Act (PA 149 of 2019, MCL 432.401–432.419), both signed 20 Dec 2019 with first launches on 22 Jan 2021; Detroit's casinos are governed by the Michigan Gaming Control and Revenue Act (1996), tribal casinos by federal IGRA compacts, and fantasy contests by the Fantasy Contests Consumer Protection Act. The MGCB (a Treasury-housed board; Executive Director Henry Williams) licenses, audits and publishes monthly operator-level results, which is why Michigan is the most transparent US iGaming dataset. Eligibility for an internet gaming or sports betting operator licence is restricted to the three Detroit casino licensees and federally recognised tribes with a Class III compact; each may contract a single platform provider, so the market is capped at 15 skins per vertical — all 15 are allocated.

**Fees are immaterial relative to tax.** An operator pays a $50,000 application fee, $100,000 on issue of the initial five-year licence and $50,000 annually thereafter (MCL 432.306(9) / 432.406(9)); platform and supplier licences are $5,000 application, $5,000 initial and $2,500 annual; fantasy operators $10,000 initial / $5,000 annual. Investigative costs can be assessed on top. For comparison, a single month of a top-three operator's iGaming tax ($10–14m) exceeds the lifetime licence fees of the entire market.

**iGaming tax is graduated on each operator's calendar-year AGR**: 20% below $4m, 22% from $4m to $8m, 24% from $8m to $10m, 26% from $10m to $12m and 28% above $12m — in practice a flat 28% since even the smallest skin (Four Winds, $16.5m AGR YTD) is above the top threshold. Detroit's three commercial operators add a 1.25% city wagering tax on AGR. The tax base is GR less free play, capped at 4% of GR in 2026 and **eliminated from 1 January 2027** for the 2021 launch cohort; the MGCB's own tax-form instructions carry the same schedule. Distribution of commercial tax is 65% Internet Gaming Fund / 5% Agriculture Equine Industry Development Fund (capped at $3m) / 30% City of Detroit; tribal payments go 70% IGF / 10% Michigan Strategic Fund / 20% to the local governing body where the tribe's casino sits. The IGF's first statutory call is a top-up to Detroit if the city's gaming taxes fall below $183m in the prior fiscal year (capped at 55% of IGF deposits less the city's 30% share), then MGCB costs, $500,000 to the Compulsive Gaming Prevention Fund, $2m to the First Responder Presumed Coverage Fund, and the balance to the School Aid Fund.

**OSB tax is 8.4% of AGR with an uncapped promo deduction**, plus 1.25% city for Detroit licensees; distribution is 65/5/30 (commercial) and 90% ISBF / 10% MSF (tribal). Fantasy contests pay 8.4% of adjusted revenues, 100% to the Fantasy Contest Fund. Detroit casinos pay 8.1% State plus 10.9% city on slots/tables and 8.4% + 1.25% on retail sports betting. The combined September 2026 public take was ~$70.8m to the State (online $62.4m + casino $8.3m + retail SB $0.03m), ~$26.8m to the City of Detroit and $8.3m to tribal governing bodies — $105.9m in a month.

**What was proposed and rejected in 2026 matters as much as what is in force.** The FY2027 executive budget (11 Feb 2026) sought a new 36% iGaming tier on annual AGR above $185m (which would have captured FanDuel, BetMGM and DraftKings; Caesars was reported just below the line at $182.1m in 2025), a $0.25/$0.50 per-wager OSB charge and the end of the OSB promo deduction, together ~$195–200m a year earmarked for the Medicaid Benefits Trust Fund. The Democratic-led Senate and Republican-led House both passed budgets without the measures (May 2026) and the enacted FY2027 budget (signed 21 Jul 2026; $75.19bn gross per NASBO) contains no gaming-tax change. The Citizens Research Council has flagged a $600–900m structural gap in that budget, Gov. Whitmer is term-limited, and preliminary results show Jocelyn Benson (D) elected governor on 3 Nov 2026. The FY2028 executive budget due in February 2027 is the next decision point; the Legislature has until 1 July 2027 to act for an October 2027 start.

**Commercial implication.** Model Michigan iGaming at 28% + (1.25% if commercial) on a base that equals GR from 2027, i.e. ~29–30% of GR all-in, and treat a move to a 30–36% top tier within two budget cycles as a material probability rather than a tail. The OSB 8.4%/uncapped-promo regime is the most generous in the US for a scaled book and the most exposed to reform; a per-wager levy at the proposed rates would have cost roughly 5–7% of 2025 OSB GR at FanDuel/DraftKings bet frequencies (our estimate), more than doubling their effective sportsbook tax.

segments.name: Enforcement, prediction markets, responsible gambling & payments
segments.headline: Michigan has become the template for state action against sports event contracts — Kalshi enjoined, Robinhood, Coinbase and Polymarket withdrawn by agreement — while running a continuous offshore cease-and-desist programme.
narrative: **Prediction markets.** The Attorney General sued KalshiEx LLC in March 2026 for offering sports-related event contracts without a Lawful Sports Betting Act licence; the Ingham County Circuit Court issued a temporary restraining order on 29 Jun 2026 (with a $120,000-per-day non-compliance penalty and a requirement to use a licensed third-party geolocation provider) and a preliminary injunction on 2 Sep 2026 requiring geofencing of Michigan. Polymarket had filed a pre-emptive federal suit against the State in March 2026; nonetheless Robinhood withdrew its sports contracts in September pending Sixth Circuit appeals, Coinbase agreed to halt on 7 Oct 2026, and on 28 Oct 2026 the MGCB announced that QCX LLC (Polymarket US) will stop offering new sports event contracts to Michigan customers and close open positions by end of day 25 Nov 2026, with enforcement stayed while it complies. Michigan is the first state to have all four major venues out by agreement or order. Federal pre-emption questions remain live in the Sixth Circuit and could reopen the channel; until then, licensed books have the sports-outcome market to themselves.

**Offshore and sweepstakes.** The MGCB issued 32 cease-and-desist letters to offshore operators on 8 Oct 2026 — the latest tranche in a programme that has run continuously since 2024 — framing the message around the absence of self-exclusion and dispute protections at unlicensed sites. Sweepstakes-casino models are treated as unlicensed gaming under MCL Chapter 432 and have been pursued through the same cease-and-desist route rather than new legislation; no dual-currency sweepstakes brand operates openly in Michigan. The practical effect for licensees is a cleaner competitive set than in most US states, which partly explains why Michigan's iGaming growth has not decelerated five years post-launch.

**Responsible gambling.** Minimum age is 21 for all MGCB-regulated verticals, with geolocation and KYC mandated at account level. Self-exclusion runs through the Internet Gaming and Sports Betting Responsible Gaming Database (online) and the Disassociated Persons List (Detroit casinos); residents can claim a free Gamban blocking licence through the MGCB; 1-800-GAMBLER and the state's 'Don't Regret the Bet' campaign appear on every release and licensee communication. Funding is statutory — $500,000 a year from each of the Internet Gaming and Internet Sports Betting Funds to the Compulsive Gaming Prevention Fund — and operators must offer deposit, wager and session limits under the MGCB's internet gaming rules [rule text not re-verified in this pass]. Advertising must carry responsible-gaming messaging and may not target under-21s [per MGCB administrative rules; wording not re-verified].

**Payments.** The MGCB does not publish deposit-method mix, limits or processing statistics (n/a). Michigan funding is card/ACH/wallet-based in the US norm; whether credit-card funding is permitted is not addressed in the sources read for this report and is marked [unverified]. There is no state-level deposit-limit mandate beyond operator-offered tools.

**Commercial implication.** Michigan's enforcement posture is an asset for licensed operators — it removes substitutes rather than adding compliance cost — but it is also the signature of a regulator and AG willing to litigate quickly. The 10 Nov 2026 Board meeting, the 25 Nov Polymarket close-out, the January 2027 free-play sunset and the February 2027 executive budget are the next four dated events.

highlights.text: Deepest regulated iGaming pool in the US and still compounding: $288.2m AGR in September (+18.4% YoY), $3.39bn trailing-12-month AGR, growth accelerating rather than fading five years after launch.

Transparent, predictable regime: monthly operator-level publication, graduated 20–28% tax unchanged since 2019, licence fees of $100k/$50k p.a. that are immaterial, and no slot/table/poker rate differential.

Lowest effective sportsbook tax among large US online states — 8.4% of AGR with uncapped promo deductions produced a State take of just 3.3% of GR in September — plus 10%+ structural hold on parlay mix.

Competitive set is being cleaned up for licensees: Kalshi enjoined, Robinhood/Coinbase/Polymarket withdrawn by agreement by 25 Nov 2026, 32 offshore C&D letters in October, sweepstakes treated as illegal — a Q4 handle tailwind and a durable moat.

Share is contestable despite the cap: Hard Rock Bet went from zero to 6.4% of iGaming AGR within nine months of relaunching on a tribal licence; FanDuel and BetMGM have ceded 6.5 points combined in a year — a platform-swap entry is proven.
Tribal skins (12 of 15 licences, 51.6% of iGaming AGR) avoid the 1.25% Detroit city levy and offer the realistic access route for a new platform partner.
Catalogue is expanding administratively — fixed-odds horse racing added to OSB on 30 Oct 2026 — signalling a regulator willing to widen product without legislation.

lowlights.text: No open licences: all 15 operator licences (3 Detroit casinos + 12 tribes) are allocated with one platform each; entry requires buying or displacing an incumbent partner, with the tribe or casino as gatekeeper.
Free-play deduction sunsets to 0% on 1 Jan 2027 under MCL 432.303(a), lifting effective iGaming tax by ~1.1pt of GR (~$40m/yr market-wide, our estimate) with no legislative action required.

A scored $195–200m/yr tax package (36% iGaming tier >$185m AGR, $0.25–0.50 per-wager OSB levy, end of OSB promo deduction) was rejected in 2026 but sits on the shelf as a new governor inherits a budget the Citizens Research Council says is $600–900m short.

OSB economics are being competed away: promo deductions ran at 48% of GR YTD (39% in 2025), YTD OSB AGR fell 6.9% despite +9.3% GR, and challengers (bet365 −$1.3m AGR, Hard Rock 93% promo/GR) are buying share at a loss.
Concentration: FanDuel + DraftKings hold 62% of OSB handle and FanDuel + BetMGM + DraftKings 61% of iGaming AGR; a sub-scale skin is a cross-sell vehicle, not a standalone business.
OSB volume has plateaued (+3.9% YoY handle in NFL kick-off month, +5.8% YTD); growth depends on hold and promo discipline, both of which are volatile month to month.

Litigation-first enforcement culture cuts both ways: the AG and MGCB move quickly against perceived unlicensed activity (TRO within three months of filing), and federal pre-emption rulings in the Sixth Circuit could reopen prediction-market competition at short notice.

forecast.intro: Nothing in Michigan's tax or licensing code changed in the September 2026 reporting period, but the trajectory did: the FY2027 executive budget's ~$200m gaming-tax package (36% iGaming top tier, per-wager OSB levy, OSB promo-deduction repeal) was stripped in May and the budget was signed on 21 Jul 2026 without it, while enforcement removed Kalshi, Robinhood, Coinbase and Polymarket from the sports-outcome market between June and October. The scheduled change is statutory — the iGaming free-play deduction drops from 4% of GR to zero on 1 January 2027 — and the unscheduled one is political: a term-limited governor hands a structurally short budget to a successor whose FY2028 proposal lands in February 2027.

forecast.view: **Market:** we expect calendar-2026 iGaming AGR of roughly $3.5–3.6bn (+20–23%) and GR of ~$3.65–3.75bn (estimates), decelerating to low-to-mid-teens growth in 2027 as the free-play sunset removes a promotional lever and the base compounds; OSB handle should stay in a +3–8% band with hold around 11–12%, so OSB AGR direction will be set by promo intensity rather than volume — we assume promos ease back toward 40% of GR once the bet365/Hard Rock share grabs normalise. **Tax:** the probability that Michigan raises iGaming and/or OSB taxes within two budget cycles is high; the specific 2026 proposal already carries a fiscal score and Michigan's 8.4% OSB rate is below every neighbour (Illinois, Ohio, Indiana). Our base case is a top-tier iGaming increase to 30–36% on the largest operators and either a per-wager charge or a promo-deduction cap on OSB effective October 2027 at the earliest, with the Detroit 1.25% levy untouched. **Licensing:** no new licences; expect one or two further platform swaps on tribal paper (Caesars Horseshoe and Four Winds are the sub-$3m/month skins most exposed). **Enforcement:** the prediction-market agreements hold unless the Sixth Circuit finds CEA pre-emption, in which case Michigan would litigate rather than accommodate. **Leverage for an entrant:** none — Michigan rewards scale and brand; a B2B/platform play supplying a tribal licensee is the lower-risk exposure.
watch: FY2028 executive budget (Feb 2027): whether Gov.-elect Benson re-tables the 36% iGaming tier, per-wager OSB levy or promo-deduction repeal, and the Senate/House response before the 1 Jul 2027 deadline.
January 2027 MGCB release (published ~Feb 2027): confirmation that iGaming GR = AGR as the free-play cap hits 0%, and any operator pullback in bonusing.
Sixth Circuit rulings on Kalshi/Coinbase/Robinhood pre-emption and Polymarket's close-out of positions by 25 Nov 2026 — any reversal reopens sports event contracts.
Q4-2026 OSB handle YoY vs the +4–6% trend as a read on how much volume the prediction-market exits return to licensed books.
Promo-deduction ratio in OSB (48% of GR YTD) — persistence above 45% into 2027 would strengthen the fiscal case for a cap.
Platform changes on the five smallest tribal skins (Caesars Horseshoe, Four Winds/Strive, Soaring Eagle/GAN, FireKeepers/NeoGames, BetPARX) — the only entry route into the market.
MGCB Board meeting 10 Nov 2026 and the Executive Director's monthly reports for rule-making on advertising, fixed-odds racing and sweepstakes enforcement.

report.confidenceNote: Market reports in USD; no FX conversion required. All headline figures (GR, AGR, handle, taxes, operator shares) are taken directly from the MGCB's 22 Oct 2026 release and its operator-level 2026/2025 Internet Gaming and Internet Sports Betting workbooks and reconcile to within $0.1m; YTD and fiscal-year aggregates are our sums of MGCB monthly data. Tax rates, fund distribution and licence fees are from the Lawful Internet Gaming Act (MCL 432.303/432.306/432.314) and the MGCB distribution chart. Items NOT verified from a primary source and flagged as such: contents of the 8 Oct 2026 cease-and-desist release (headline only), the MGCB Executive Director's September 2026 report, advertising-rule wording, payment-method rules (credit-card funding) and statistics (n/a), tribal land-based casino revenue (not published), the $182.1m Caesars 2025 AGR figure (OddsShark), the 2026 governor election result (preliminary, MultiState/DDHQ), and the calendar-2026 and free-play-sunset dollar impacts, which are our estimates.
